subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-disabled `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` config key plus a shared `onTaskTimeout` command-queue hook as the permanent compatibility boundary for bounding deferred context-engine maintenance?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but the new operator config and shared queue callback become supported API/behavior once merged, and automation should not decide that product contract.

options.title: Accept the opt-in timeout contract
options.body: Merge after maintainer confirmation that a default-disabled config key and shared queue timeout hook are the desired boundary for this stall class.

options.title: Narrow the queue API first
options.body: Replace the shared onTaskTimeout callback with a more local maintenance-owned mechanism if maintainers do not want to grow the queue contract.

options.title: Pause for broader policy design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want burst coalescing or shorter interactive recovery handled in the same design before landing.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in timeout contract
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainer confirmation that a default-disabled config key and shared queue timeout hook are the desired boundary for this stall class.

likelyOwner.reason: They appear in the feature history as context-engine transcript maintenance owner and reviewer/co-author of the background maintenance path.
